note: Ceiling for internal/controlplane, in hand-written non-test Go lines. Build-ignored tools and generated DO-NOT-EDIT output are reported but not counted; see scripts/report-migration-progress.mjs. The bounded-context migration may only move this down. Raising it requires saying why in the same commit.
reason: Raised by 23 for #25, the display half of the Intermittent agents setting. The rule -- an aged report from an environment whose gaps are expected is shown with its age but not counted stale -- lives in internal/reporting/domain (FleetQuery.SilenceExpected and one clause in BuildFleet). What is here is expectedSilenceEnvironments, which classifies the fleet's environments from the plans the overview has already loaded; it must be here because it reads PlanRecord and resolves federation, both this context's, and it deliberately uses the loaded snapshot rather than a repository read per environment so the overview stays one bounded snapshot. The behavioural half of #25 needed no code: #15 already made ParticipatesInPromotion include intermittent, so an intermittent environment already vouches, and the operator's MaximumEvidenceAgeSeconds bound is correctly left alone. The previous 24438 was recorded on 2026-08-16 and read: Raised by 9 for #13, the reviewer-requirement satisfiability diagnostic. The substance -- computing whether any current grant could satisfy a requirement, and the reason text -- lives in internal/governance/application (Authorizer.RequirementSatisfiable and AnnotateSatisfiability); an earlier draft that put the loop in controlplane cost 27 lines and was moved out, recovering 18. What remains here is the read-path hook alone: annotateSatisfiability decorates a ChangeRequest before the GET handler serializes it. It cannot leave this context because ChangeRequest and the HTTP mux are controlplane's, exactly like the Apollo GraphQL mount below. The previous 24429 was recorded on 2026-08-15 and read: Lowered by 7. session.go held a hand-maintained copy of the eleven operation constants, which is now governance.OperationVocabulary aliased through governance_alias.go -- one list instead of two, so a session cannot advertise a capability the domain does not declare. The previous 24436 was recorded on 2026-08-15 and read: Raised by 84 for the Apollo GraphQL mount. This is the first rise since the bounded-context migration, and it is wiring rather than behaviour: apollo_graphql.go builds the resolver, binds one request's sources from the authenticated principal, and registers two routes. It cannot live in internal/apollographql because it needs Repository, GovernanceService, HandlerOptions and requireOperatorPrincipal, all of which are this context's -- moving it would mean exporting the monolith's internals to a package that exists to depend on none of them. Fourteen of the 84 lines are newOverviewSource, extracted so the GraphQL interface and the console's overview build one reader's snapshot through one constructor; two constructions could authorize differently, which is exactly the drift Reporting's port comment warns against. Everything the interface actually decides -- the served contract, its provenance, what may be answered and what must be refused -- is 1,200 lines in internal/apollographql and none of it is here. The previous 24352 was recorded on 2026-08-15 for the Execution slice, on the same counting basis.
